To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the density profile in a driven reaction–diffusion system relaxes exponentially fast to a steady state, (ii) the steady state density profile is a smooth function of the driving force, (iii) the density correlation function in the steady state decays as a power law with a power law exponent that depends on the driving force.
the diffusion–annihilation model in 1D, when subject to a driving field, has a nontrivial steady state that is characterized by a nontrivial density profile.
the reaction–diffusion process is equivalent to the motion of free fermions and the fermion representation allows the calculation of all correlation functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of a one‐dimensional lattice gas of hard core particles with a nearest neighbor exclusion interaction and with a nearest neighbor attractive interaction.
the study of the dynamics of a one dimensional lattice gas of hard core particles, which undergoes nearest‐neighbor annihilation with a rate one, and nearest‐neighbor hopping with a rate 1/2.
the study of the diffusion–annihilation reaction in one‐dimensional lattices.

the diffusion–annihilation dynamics of the driven system is a very interesting and complex phenomenon, and the field theoretical approach provides a useful tool for its analysis.
the model under consideration is a very good candidate to be used in experiments to investigate the diffusion–annihilation problem.
the model under consideration is not exactly solvable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to calculate all the time‐dependent density and density‐density correlation functions of this model.
the dynamics of a driven system with an uncorrelated initial state can be described in a simple way in terms of free Fermi fields.
the diffusion–annihilation model in one dimension can be solved exactly in terms of free Fermi fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the diffusion–annihilation model in one dimension can be used as a model for the diffusion and annihilation of a gas of particles with an external driving force in the presence of a potential barrier.
the fermion approach is a very useful tool in the study of nonequilibrium dynamics of reaction–diffusion systems.
a random initial density profile evolves to a nontrivial steady state in the presence of the external force.
